description: Every engine item that SinkBroom's lit preview mirrors, or deliberately does not copy, with the engine commit it was read at. Checked before each landing by TOOLS/lit_mirror_check.py (LP-M).

rules.lines: first and last line, 1-based and inclusive, in the file at engineCommit
rules.anchor: the function, member or symbol that holds the range, for finding it again once the engine's line numbers move
rules.sha256: of the range's text at engineCommit: each line without its line ending, followed by \n
rules.sinkbroom: the SinkBroom file and symbol that mirror the range or say why not

kinds.dispatcher: the vulkan.hpp dynamic dispatcher's storage and initialisation
kinds.instance: a property of the Vulkan instance
kinds.device-extension: a device extension and the code that enables it
kinds.feature-chain: device features that are checked and enabled
kinds.function: engine code mirrored with the stated differences
kinds.constant: an engine value used as is
kinds.not-copied: engine code deliberately not mirrored, with the reason
kinds.copied-file: an engine file copied whole and byte for byte into lib/TbLitLib/idtech/engine; gitBlob is its git blob id at engineCommit
kinds.copied-range: engine line ranges copied verbatim into a partial file under lib/TbLitLib/idtech/engine, each preceded by one marker line
kinds.build: how TbLitIdLib is compiled: the engine's C++ standard and the compile definitions the copied files branch on
kinds.table: an engine table mirrored row for row
kinds.shim-virtual: a virtual of a copied or engine class that the shim defines, so the vtables link
kinds.fatal-site: a never-returning engine call (Error, FatalError) in the copied or mirrored code, which the shim turns into log-and-return, with what the code does after it returns
kinds.static: a static or global of the copied code (or the shim's bindings), its kind and why it needs no reset
kinds.temporary: a stand-in that a later package replaces
kinds.guard: a check outside the copied code that keeps a latent engine fault from being reached
kinds.difference: a deliberate difference from the engine's behaviour, with its reason
kinds.known-defect: an engine defect the copy keeps verbatim, with its effect
kinds.pure-function: copied engine code that the facade lets any thread run, because it touches no state

entries.note: vulkan.hpp's default dynamic dispatcher: storage defined once, initialised from vkGetInstanceProcAddr and the instance (initInstanceDispatcher, on every Start) and from the device (createVkDevice). The engine loads the library itself; SinkBroom takes vkGetInstanceProcAddr from Qt (C9).
Vulkan 1.2 instance (S12), through QVulkanInstance::setApiVersion.
Required: VK_KHR_swapchain (only when presenting; the headless test path does not need it) and VK_KHR_maintenance1.

Optional VK_KHR_synchronization2 with VkPhysicalDeviceSynchronization2FeaturesKHR::synchronization2 chained after the 1.2 features. It switches NVRHI's barriers to vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 (nvrhi vulkan-state-tracking.cpp:345), so the preview takes the game's barrier path. Dropped when the extension is listed but the feature is not.
Optional VK_EXT_memory_budget, the VRAM budget's source (S9, LP2).

VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures: shaderImageGatherExtended, samplerAnisotropy, textureCompressionBC, imageCubeArray, dualSrcBlend on; shaderStorageImageReadWithoutFormat, tessellationShader, geometryShader, fillModeNonSolid as supported. The five forced features are checked at device choice (the engine checks only samplerAnisotropy and textureCompressionBC there; the others would fail vkCreateDevice).

VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features in DeviceCreateInfo::pNext: descriptorIndexing, runtimeDescriptorArray, descriptorBindingPartiallyBound, descriptorBindingVariableDescriptorCount, timelineSemaphore (NVRHI's queue tracking), shaderSampledImageArrayNonUniformIndexing; each is checked at device choice.

pickPhysicalDevice: per device the required extensions, features, B8G8R8A8_UNORM surface format, FIFO and present support; the first discrete GPU, else the first other device, in enumeration order. Added: Vulkan 1.2 or newer (S12), and the error text lists every device with its problems instead of FatalError. Changed: the surface's formats and present modes are asked only of a device with a family that presents to the surface, as the specification requires, and a device whose queries throw is skipped with a log line instead of ending the choice (review L3.3).

findQueueFamilies and the queue create infos. The engine takes the first graphics family and the first present family separately and may create two queues; the preview requires one family that does both, creates one queue and keeps the swapchain images exclusive.
Timer queries only when timestampPeriod > 0 and the family's timestampValidBits > 0; otherwise the frame log's GPU column stays empty.

nvrhi::vulkan::DeviceDesc with the enabled instance and device extensions, graphics queue only; nvrhi::validation::createValidationLayer in Debug with SessionOptions::validation (the engine: r_useValidationLayers). errorCB is the session's own callback, which counts errors and sets the lost flag (R5.19), instead of DefaultMessageCallback, which turns errors into FatalError.
Swapchain format RGBA8_UNORM swapped to B8G8R8A8_UNORM. The engine always pairs it with SRGB_NONLINEAR; the preview takes the colour space of the surface's matching format entry.
Swapchain image count NUM_FRAME_DATA = 3, clamped to the surface's minImageCount and maxImageCount (0 = no limit).

VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR: usage ColorAttachment | TransferDst | Sampled, one array layer, identity pre-transform, opaque composite alpha, clipped, no old swapchain. The preview falls back to the current transform and the first supported alpha mode when identity or opaque is not offered, and always uses exclusive sharing (one family).
Swapchain image wrappers: createHandleForNativeTexture(VK_Image) with initialState Present, keepInitialState, isRenderTarget.

The engine clamps its back-buffer size into the surface's range. The preview uses currentExtent, takes the passed window size only when currentExtent is 0xFFFFFFFF, and makes no swapchain for 0×0 (§3.1).

The engine's r_swapInterval / r_vkPreferFastSync choice among MAILBOX, IMMEDIATE, FIFO_RELAXED and FIFO. The preview uses MAILBOX if offered, else FIFO, and FIFO when forced (D48, R5.4); IMMEDIATE only if LP0 measures FIFO's present blocking beyond a bound.

The engine acquires with an infinite timeout and asserts on the result, and cycles one semaphore per image for both acquire and present. The preview acquires with a 50 ms timeout (D48) through the vk::Result overloads, skips on TIMEOUT or NOT_READY, posts SwapchainOutOfDate on OUT_OF_DATE or SUBOPTIMAL, and keeps acquire semaphores per frame in flight and present semaphores per image, all owned by the swapchain generation.

The engine's single frame event query, waited per NUM_FRAME_DATA. The preview keeps a ring of kFramesInFlight event queries and waits on frame N - 2's before recording frame N (D35). The wait polls the event query and ends on a stop or a park, where NVRHI's waitEventQuery would wait without a bound (review L2.1).

Optional device extensions and features the preview does not need: VK_EXT_debug_marker (debug utils replaces it), VK_EXT_descriptor_indexing (its features are core 1.2 and enabled through VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features), VK_KHR_buffer_device_address and bufferDeviceAddress (ray tracing only; the engine notes it 'only makes problems'), VK_NV_mesh_shader, VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate and its features, VK_KHR_format_feature_flags2, VK_GOOGLE_display_timing and hostQueryReset (Optick), the ray-tracing extensions, the macOS portability subset.

Instance extensions: VK_KHR_get_physical_device_properties2 (core since 1.1; the instance is 1.2), VK_EXT_sampler_filter_minmax (listed by the engine as an instance extension, but it is a device extension and its feature is never enabled), VK_EXT_debug_report and its callback (replaced by VK_EXT_debug_utils, which Qt adds for its debug output redirect when the session validates; the tests' own instance asks for it itself). Qt adds the surface extensions.
The VK_LAYER_MESSAGE_ID_FILTER environment variable: a process-wide setting; LP0 creates no pipelines, whose warnings it filters. Revisit when pipelines arrive (LP2).
The D24S8 format probe, the VMA allocator, the push-constant size and Optick's GPU init: not used by LP0. The push-constant size and the depth format come with the passes (LP2, C2).
Compute and transfer queues: the preview submits everything, uploads included, on the graphics queue (S35).

The engine's destruction order (waitIdle, semaphores, swapchain, device handle, VkDevice, surface, instance) never collects NVRHI garbage. The preview follows §3.1's teardown steps instead: release handles, waitForIdle, runGarbageCollection (skipped when lost), wrappers, vkDestroySwapchainKHR, semaphores, the NVRHI device with its last Release() count, then the VkDevice; the surface and the instance belong to Qt.

linkOptions.name: /OPT:REF
linkOptions.when: MSVC Release links of every target that links TbLitLib, only with TB_ENABLE_LIT_PREVIEW (an INTERFACE option of the static TbLitLib: TbLitLibTest, and through TbUiLib the final links of TrenchBroom.exe, DumpShortcuts and TbUiLibTest)
linkOptions.why: G12: TrenchBroom.exe's Release link passes /DEBUG (app/TrenchBroom/CMakeLists.txt), whose default is /OPT:NOREF, so the copied Str.cpp's six thread_local buffers (192 KB, M-ID-STATIC-30..35) stayed in its static TLS although nothing calls their functions. The other links have no /DEBUG and drop them already. It removes every library's unreferenced code from TrenchBroom.exe, not only Str.cpp's: the user decides whether that stays (14-LP1A-FIXES-2.md D); if not, the options go and the 192 KB are recorded as accepted

linkOptions.name: /OPT:NOICF
linkOptions.when: MSVC Release links of every target that links TbLitLib, only with TB_ENABLE_LIT_PREVIEW (an INTERFACE option of the static TbLitLib: TbLitLibTest, and through TbUiLib the final links of TrenchBroom.exe, DumpShortcuts and TbUiLibTest)
linkOptions.why: W.8 (round 2): an explicit /OPT:REF also folds identical functions (/OPT:ICF) unless /OPT:NOICF is given. Folded functions share one address, so a cpptrace stack trace from the stripped PDB can name the folded twin, and pointer-to-member comparisons of identical bodies compare equal (Qt's PMF-based disconnect). NOICF keeps every function apart; in the links without /DEBUG it turns off the folding they had by default

entries.tls: the six thread_local buffers of the copied Str.cpp (M-ID-STATIC-30..35, three 4 x MAX_PRINT_MSG buffers, 192 KB) are static TLS in every thread of a binary that keeps them; the copy never calls their functions. dumpbin /tls, raw data (G12, 2026-10-21): TrenchBroom.exe Release before LP1a 0x273C, a Release link of the LP1a.2 state 0x3276C (+0x30030: kept, because TrenchBroom's Release link passes /DEBUG, which turns /OPT:REF off), TbUiLibTest Release 0x2891 (linked without /DEBUG, so /OPT:REF drops them), TbLitLibTest Debug 0x39DA4, TrenchBroom.exe Debug 0x3CAE3. Fix (linkOptions): /OPT:REF /OPT:NOICF on every MSVC Release link that uses TbLitLib. Measured at round 2 (W.8): TrenchBroom.exe Release 0x273C and 21,978,112 bytes (with /OPT:REF alone, folding: 0x273C and 19,984,384 bytes; without either, 41.5 MB), TbUiLibTest Release 0x2891, TrenchBroom.exe Debug 0x3CAE3. Debug keeps the buffers: accepted

ReadFile returns a Mem_Alloc'ed, NUL-terminated buffer of length + 1, -1 and FILE_NOT_FOUND_TIMESTAMP for an unreadable file. Not in the engine (R5.20): once the registry's cancel flag is set, every later ReadFile returns an empty file without asking the source, so the copied RegisterDeclFolder loop ends after the file it was reading and nothing is reported. D63: common and idLib::common point to one idCommon, tbLitCommonSink, from the start of the process and are never rebound; its Printf, Warning, Error and FatalError (and idLib's message functions, AssertFailed and the file system's warnings) format the message on the calling thread and push it, tagged with that thread, into one queue under a mutex. Constant-initialised: the queue's constructor is constexpr (std::mutex, two null node pointers and a count), and it allocates a node only when a message is pushed (C9, S27); nodes still queued at exit are not freed. Pushing never throws (C17): a node that cannot be allocated is lost, and a lost Error or FatalError is counted in lostErrors, which every registry's errorCount adds. The registry drains its own thread's messages (Registry::messages, takeMessages, errorCount, beginCapture, endCapture) and drops those its thread pushed before it was made and while it is destroyed, as no registry received them before; any other thread's are drained by that thread's owner with drainEngineMessagesForThread (the CPU pool's, LP1b.2). MakeNameCanonical writes one byte past its MAX_STRING_CHARS buffer for a name of MAX_STRING_CHARS or more characters without a '.' among them. A map face can pass one to the facade, which refuses such names; canonicalName uses a buffer one byte longer. The copied code can pass one too, from a decl file (a decl name in LoadAndParse, an inherit value, a table, particle or skin reference): M-ID-GUARD-06 keeps such files from being parsed (A2.5, A3.9)

entries.note: ParseStage warns at the 257th stage but does not return, and writes past pd->parseStages[256] on the parse thread's stack (A2.4; the engine at the pinned commit has the same defect). After numStages++ it also writes a coverage stage at parseStages[numStages] with no limit check when the stage is diffuse and alpha-tested (engine Material.cpp:2298-2302, the copy's 2299-2303), so one call can write two slots. Before anything can parse it, every material decl whose text can make more than 256 slots is made the default material, with the engine's warning, and its lookup fails with that reason. The bound comes from the copied idLexer's tokens with DECL_LEXER_FLAGS (forEachDeclToken, the tokens idMaterial::Parse reads): after the first "{" (SkipUntilString), every token equal to "{" counts 1 and every stage shortcut keyword 2, whatever its type and wherever it stands. ParseMaterial calls ParseStage only for such a token, once per token. A stage is diffuse only through ParseBlend's diffusemap or basecolormap: in a "{" block that is a token of the material's text, counted 2, which pays for the block's coverage slot; a shortcut's stage is parsed from synthesised text holding its image name without the quotes (AppendToken), so diffusemap "_white alphaTest 0.5" makes two slots that its second count pays for. AddImplicitStages adds at most one stage, below the limit, without an alpha test. So the bound is never below the slots the engine writes; it is above them where such a token is an argument, a block's own keyword or text after a parse error (M-ID-DIFF-03). W.1 (round 2) replaced a character scan of brace depth that crafted text got past ('diffusemap {', 'qer_editorimage {', the lexer's '/*/' comment, '.5diffusemap'); X.1 (round 3) counts shortcuts twice for the coverage stage

a decl file holding a token of MAX_STRING_CHARS or more characters with no '.' among the first MAX_STRING_CHARS is refused with a warning and read as unreadable (the copied LoadAndParse then reports 'couldn't load'), because any token can reach MakeNameCanonical and overflow its buffer. The tokens are the copied idLexer's with DECL_LEXER_FLAGS over the whole file (forEachDeclToken, which silences only the lexer's printing with LEXFL_NOERRORS and LEXFL_NOWARNINGS and goes on after a token it cannot read wherever the lexer moved forward; the decl parsers go on there too, while LoadAndParse stops at a failed top-level read, so the scan reads a superset of the tokens the engine reads), so strings joined across a backslash, '...' literals with spaces, a name after a number and the lexer's comment rules are read exactly as the engine reads them; tokens inside comments are not tokens. A dot ends the canonical name first, so the retail PDAs' long texts are read (newpdas/enpro_hammer.pda: a 1075-character string whose first dot is its fifth character). A known difference: the engine reads such a file and overruns. W.1 (round 2) replaced a character scan of names and quoted strings that crafted text got past
as M-ID-GUARD-01, for the console-command functions: a name of MAX_STRING_CHARS or more characters is refused before FindType or PrintType canonicalises it

the bulk parse's index functions check the index against GetNumDecls before DeclByIndex; evaluate also refuses an entry whose registry id is not this registry's, so an entry of an earlier build never reaches DeclByIndex
DeclByIndex reads past its list after reporting an out-of-range index; the facade checks an entry's index against GetNumDecls and its name before calling it

a folder's files with an extension over every source, in GetFileList's order: the resource files (searchPaths and containers from the last), each in its table's order, then the .pk4 files the same way, then the loose files; a container entry only when it lies directly in the folder (allowSubdirsForResourcePaks is false), with GetFileList's own tests, case-insensitively, its trailing slashes stripped. AddUnique keeps the first spelling (containers store lowercased names); the shim's ListFiles adds each once and sorts with idSort_PathStr (the copied IcmpPath)

the containers of <game path>/base in registration order: Sys_ListFiles( base, ".resources" ) sorted with idSort_PathStr, then Sys_ListFiles( base/maps, ".resources" ) sorted, each with "maps/" in front; then Sys_ListFiles( base, ".pk4" ) sorted. A .pk4 holding binary.conf is refused without a message, as Init refuses it. A container whose Init fails is skipped with the engine's warning. On Windows the first listing recurses and lists base/maps' containers too; the engine then registers them twice, and SinkBroom keeps each once at its later place, which finds the same file for every name (M-FS-DIFF-04). With fs_resourceLoadPriority 0, a read searches each kind from the last registered: base/maps' .resources (z to a), then base's (z to a); .pk4 files z to a

fs_resourceLoadPriority 0 (its default): the loose file first, then the .pk4 files, then the resource files, each kind searched from its last registered container (M-FS-02). A leading slash is dropped; a path holding .. or ::, or an empty one, finds nothing; a container lookup refuses a path with a colon (an OS path), and compares the path with backslashes made slashes, case-insensitively. A container's file has time 0 (the engine wraps it in an idFile_Memory); a loose file's time is its modification time

the header (big-endian magic 0xD000000D, table offset, table length), the table (big-endian count; per entry a little-endian name length, the name, big-endian offset and length; a negative name length reads no name), names with backslashes made slashes and ASCII lowercased (CharIsUpper also accepts 0xC0-0xDF, but char is signed in the engine's builds), the later of two entries with one name first (Add puts the newer at the head of its chain), an entry's bytes at offset. Not in the engine: every offset and length is checked against the file before it is read (M-FS-DIFF-03)

a .pk4's entries as Init stores them, backslashes made slashes and lowercased, read through TrenchBroom's ZipFileSystem (D55), which skips directory entries (GetFileList skips them too) and keeps the later of two entries whose names differ only in case (ImageFileSystemBase::addFile), as the engine's hash finds it; an entry is read with ZipFileSystem::openFile

on Windows the folder and every folder below it, names relative to the folder with forward slashes, a file's long name matched by PathMatchSpecW against *<extension> (a case-insensitive suffix); elsewhere the folder alone, fnmatch( *<extension>, name, 0 ) (case-sensitive) and no directory. So on Windows a loose decl file in a subfolder of materials is read, as the engine reads it. Not in the engine: a folder that cannot be read lists nothing and the others are still listed (each folder has its own iterator); a name that is not valid Unicode is skipped, with a warning when it is a folder or matches the extension (G3); the listing stops within one directory entry once the cancel flag is set (G4)

a loose file at <game path>/base/<path>; on POSIX, when the path does not open, the file in the same folder whose path equals it case-insensitively. Opened with share-read, share-write and share-delete on Windows, where the engine shares read only (M-FS-DIFF-02)

C1: one search path, <game path>/base, from Map::gamePath(). No mod, fs_game, fs_game_base or fs_savepath is searched: the engine adds fs_savepath after fs_basepath and each mod after base, and searches the newest first

R4-3.26, A2.15: loose and .resources files are opened per read batch with share-read, share-write and share-delete, so the user can save or replace them while the preview runs; every container closes at the end of the batch. A .pk4 is opened by TbFsLib's createCFile (_wfopen, which shares read and write but not delete) for its batch only: TbFsLib is not changed (C12)

a container that the engine would quit on (a wrong magic, FatalError) or read out of bounds (a header, table or entry that does not fit in the file) is refused, or the entry dropped, with a warning; a container that changed after its table was read is not read from. A name is cut at its first NUL, as the engine's C-string lookups see it
a container listed twice (base/maps on Windows) is registered once, at its later place; the engine opens it twice, and its earlier copy never finds a file that the later one does not find first

a reload builds a new registry from a new source (the containers are scanned again) instead of the engine's per-file Reload, and re-parses the names the consumers asked for before it publishes; only loose decl folders are polled (R4-3.26). G5, G6 (A2.3, A3.5, A3.6): the loose decl files' times, unreadable ones included, are stamped before and after each build; a build whose stamps differ, or whose source read a loose file that kept changing (stat before and after each read, three attempts), asks for one more build, and a change found by a poll does too, at most once per autoReloadInterval (5 s). A file that lists but cannot be read is reported once (the copied 'couldn't load') and builds nothing until its time changes; case-differing loose duplicates on POSIX stamp alike before and after, so they never loop

A3.11: AddUnique hashes case-sensitively, so a loose Foo.mtr and a container's foo.mtr are both listed; RegisterDeclFolder folds them with Icmp but runs LoadAndParse twice, which is idempotent and reports its warnings twice. SinkBroom folds case-insensitively and keeps the first spelling (the container's lowercase one), so a material's source file can differ in case. No decl content differs; retail has no uppercase decl file names

A3.8: the engine's FindFirstFileW recursion follows a directory junction or link (FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY); SinkBroom does not follow one, so a junctioned folder below base/materials is neither read nor polled. Carried to LP1c

A3.13: TbFsLib's ZipFileSystem decodes a .pk4 entry name in the ANSI code page on Windows, so a non-ASCII entry name differs from the engine's raw bytes (another sort place, no fold with a loose file of that name); an entry whose name is not valid Unicode is skipped with a warning (G3). Carried to LP1c

A2.8, kept verbatim: a videomap, soundmap or stencil stage that a later error leaves before numStages++ (or a second one in one stage) leaks its cinematic or stencil block, because FreeData frees stages[0..numStages) only; once per malformed decl and build, as in the engine. Retail's 15 defaulted materials were not traced for it

A3.10, carried to LP1c: the engine loads a new image record at once, and the load can rewrite its usage (R_LoadImageProgram, the _rmao rename), which a later lookup with the first usage then does not match; the shim loads nothing, so MaterialImageKey::usage is the requested usage, not the engine's #__UUCC digits. A record is found case-insensitively and keeps the spelling and parameters of the material that made it first; the engine's creation order (start-up, map load) and SinkBroom's (lookups, the bulk parse) differ, so a name's case and a _name's parameters can differ. The goldens compare the usage digits of every image the engine failed to load, and the editor images case-insensitively

entries.note: W.1, X.1 (rounds 2 and 3): M-ID-GUARD-05 refuses a material when the "{" tokens after its first, plus twice its stage shortcut keyword tokens, exceed MAX_SHADER_STAGES (256), wherever those tokens stand; the engine's own slot count cannot be had without running the parser that overruns. The engine parses a material whose stages plus coverage stages are at most 256. Engine-parsable materials this refuses: more than 128 shortcut lines without an alpha-tested diffuse image name (the engine takes up to 256); more than 85 stage blocks that name their interaction with a shortcut keyword ('blend diffusemap', 'blend bumpmap', 'blend specularmap', 'blend rmaomap' and their aliases, ParseBlend), each counted 3, where the engine takes up to 256 (128 alpha-tested diffuse ones); any mix of blocks and shortcuts whose count passes 256 while the slots do not (254 plain blocks and one shortcut count 256 and parse; 255 and one count 257 and are refused, though the engine writes 256 slots); and a material whose arguments, or whose text after a parse error, hold such tokens. Tested: 85 interaction blocks parse and 86 are refused; 128 shortcuts with an alpha-tested image name parse to 256 stages and 129 are refused; one plain block and 128 such shortcuts are refused. No retail material is refused

A2.16: the two facade functions any thread may call, though they run copied code (C20 otherwise keeps copied code on the parse thread): both read only their arguments and write only their result (IcmpPath's Printf is under #if 0). GameDeclSource calls compareEnginePaths on the thread that makes it

D63: the sink formats every message with the copied vsnPrintf on the calling thread, into a MAX_PRINT_MSG buffer on that thread's stack, as the registry-bound common did, so a message reads the same whichever thread reports it. vsnPrintf reads only its arguments and writes only dest; it calls no idLib function
